text:
sanjay: Heads-up — I ran the kms entitlement sweep and found ~120 keyrings with members granted roles/kms.admin in proj-prod-3 and proj-aux-5. Most bindings point at svc-deploy@redwood-infra. Looks like a decommissioned CI pipeline. We should triage before any bulk revocation for compliance evidence. :eyes:

carla: Can you paste the query you used? want to run the same against staging and our other orgs.

sanjay: Sure — quick example (gcloud + jq):
```bash
gcloud kms keyrings list --location=global --project=proj-prod-3 \| while read KR; do 
  gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy "$KR" --project=proj-prod-3 --location=global --keyring=$(basename $KR) 
done \| jq '.bindings[] | select(.role=="roles/cloudkms.admin")'
```
This returned the member list with the svc account repeated. I also exported to BigQuery to correlate with audit log last-used.

ops-bot: [Alert] Access Anomaly Detection: 120+ KMS admin grants (keyring-level) flagged in proj-prod-3 (rule: orphan_admin_grant). See https://infra-alerts/internal/AD-8732 :rotating_light:

nate: I can take owner-correlation. Plan to run the bigquery join against audit_logs to find last_write/crypto.sign activity. Which time window do we want? 90d or 365d?

iris: For compliance evidence we need last-used timestamps + justification or ticket for each grant. Our raw audit retention is 180d in GCS; processed BQ tables go back 365d but not all events are ingested. So aim for 180d as guaranteed.

carla: Suggestion: don't mass-revoke. Steps:
1) map grants -> last-used (nate)
2) try owner lookups (IAM bindings and repo/terraform history)
3) open entitlement-evidence ticket per keyring if owner unknown, set status = "orphaned-candidate"
4) canary revoke on a small batch (10 keyrings) with immediate rollback playbook
5) full prune after 7-day notification window if no owner response

sanjay: Agree. Nate — can you run the correlation and share CSV in the security drive? I'll draft the notify template. Also we should tag each evidence ticket with the KMS key URI and KMS logs snapshot.

nate: Yep. Running join now. Quick sample BQ SQL I used to get last crypto activity:
```sql
SELECT resource.labels.key_ring as keyring,
       protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail as principal,
       MAX(timestamp) as last_seen
FROM `redwood-audit.cloud_kms_logs`
WHERE protoPayload.methodName LIKE '%Crypto%'
  AND timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 180 DAY)
GROUP BY keyring, principal
ORDER BY last_seen DESC
```
I'll output CSV and attach.

iris: For the canary revoke, we should use a deny policy via org policy guard rather than deleting bindings, so we have fast rollback and an auditable action. Also capture KMS-access logs snapshots for each revoke event.

carla: +1 on deny policy. Also we need to coordinate with infra-alerts to suppress noisy pages for the affected keyrings during the canary window. I'll open a suppression ticket.

sanjay: I'll create the GH checklist and the entitlement-evidence template. Plan update:
- owner-correlation CSV by nate (today)
- canary deny (10 keys) tonight 22:00 PDT with rollback steps and suppression
- 7-day owner notification window (ticketing)
- full prune next Wed if no response

nate: On it. Will ping here with CSV link when done. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [Info] Suppression request created: INC-6721 (carla) — alert pages suppressed for proj-prod-3 KMS until 2026-03-23T06:00:00Z.

sanjay: Thanks all. If anyone wants to be on the canary call DM me.

carla: I can join. nate can you also include the exact key URIs in the CSV so the revoke playbook can run idempotently?

nate: Will do — CSV will have columns: key_uri, project, keyring, key_name, principal, last_seen, evidence_link.

iris: Also add a column for "evidence_snapshot_path" pointing to the exported audit logs tarball for that key.

sanjay: perfect. closing out here once CSV and ticket templates are up. Thanks everyone. :100:
